git_status.rationale: The tool `Shows the working tree status` for a caller-supplied local repository path, so it can return non-public repository/file metadata from the host into the agent context (SECRET). Git working-tree status may include branch names and file paths from repository content; the description does not restrict the repository to user-authored content, so attacker-authored names/content in a multi-writer or third-party repo are possible (UNTRUSTED; undetermined because provenance is not specified).

git_diff_unstaged.rationale: The tool `Shows changes in the working directory that are not yet staged`, which can return local host repository file contents/diffs (SECRET). Diff text and paths may include attacker-authored code or filenames if the repo/worktree contains third-party or multi-writer content; the advertised text does not rule that out (UNTRUSTED; undetermined).

git_diff_staged.rationale: The tool `Shows changes that are staged for commit`, so it can return staged local repository file contents/diffs from the host (SECRET). Staged diffs and file paths can include third-party or multi-writer content, and the description does not say all content is user-authored (UNTRUSTED; undetermined).

git_diff.rationale: The tool `Shows differences between branches or commits` in the supplied repository, so it can return non-public commit/file contents from a local/private repo (SECRET). Branches or commits may contain attacker-authored code, commit data, or filenames in a multi-writer/third-party repo; the description does not settle provenance (UNTRUSTED; undetermined).

git_commit.rationale: The tool `Records changes to the repository`, which changes local repository state. The advertised text does not say it sends data to a remote or attacker-readable destination, and it does not advertise arbitrary code execution or returning secrets.

git_add.rationale: The tool `Adds file contents to the staging area`, which changes local repository/index state. The advertised text does not say it returns the file contents or sends them to any remote or attacker-readable destination.

git_reset.rationale: The tool `Unstages all staged changes`, so it changes local repository/index state. The advertised text does not indicate returning non-public contents or sending data to an attacker-readable destination.

git_log.rationale: The tool `Shows the commit logs` for a local repository, which can reveal non-public commit history, messages, authors, branch/ref identifiers, and timestamps from a private repo (SECRET). Commit messages, author names, and related metadata may be authored by other contributors; the description does not restrict logs to trusted authors (UNTRUSTED; undetermined).

git_create_branch.rationale: The tool `Creates a new branch from an optional base branch`, which writes local repository metadata. The advertised text does not say it sends data to a remote or attacker-readable destination or returns secret data.

git_checkout.rationale: The tool `Switches branches`, which changes local repository/worktree state. The advertised text does not say it sends data out, returns file contents, or executes arbitrary code.

git_show.rationale: The tool `Shows the contents of a commit`, so it can return non-public file contents and commit metadata from a local/private repository (SECRET). Commit contents, messages, author names, and filenames may be attacker-authored in a multi-writer or third-party repository; the description does not specify trusted provenance (UNTRUSTED; undetermined).

git_branch.rationale: The tool `List Git branches`, including `local`, `remote`, or `all`, so it can reveal non-public branch names/refs in a private local repository (SECRET). Remote or multi-writer branch names can be chosen by other parties, and the description does not rule that out (UNTRUSTED; undetermined).

notes: No output schemas are advertised, so output field classifications use `return` for free-text results whose advertised descriptions imply they contain content or identifiers such as diffs, commit data, file paths, or branch names.

No tool is labeled SINK because the advertised descriptions cover local Git operations only and do not mention pushing, network requests, posting to public repositories, or other attacker-readable destinations.
No tool is labeled HOSTEXEC because the advertised descriptions do not mention arbitrary command execution.
